claims.label: Unattended Items Seized Near Library Bus Stop
claims.claim: In a hearing clip the host plays, Sergeant Faumuina testifies that officers canvassing the scene found unattended items at the bus stops by the library (Folsom Library in the clip) and seized a backpack, a jacket and gloves, and possibly other items she does not recall.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain hearing transcript or video exhibits to verify item count (three vs. nine) and chain of custody.

claims.label: Clip Shows Sergeant Faumuina Not Remembering Telling the FBI Lab to Stop Testing
claims.claim: In a hearing clip the host plays, Sergeant Faumuina agrees that the seized items were sent to the FBI lab, and when asked whether she eventually told the lab the items were not connected to the case and needed no further testing, says she does not remember communicating that.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain FBI/ATF lab correspondence and UVU communications log for the testing discontinuation instruction.

claims.label: Anonymous Eyewitness Says Rooftop Person Used Tactical Movement Pattern
claims.claim: In a September 25 recording the host plays, the anonymous eyewitness says the rooftop person moved in what looked like a tactical movement, going down to look around, then standing and running about 6 feet forward, and was in view for about 30 seconds in total, taking about 10 seconds to reach the spot where he lay down to shoot.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare witness description to rooftop video exhibits and to expert definitions of Individual Movement Technique (IMT).

claims.label: Eyewitness Described All-Black Tactical Attire and Face Mask
claims.claim: In a recording the host plays, the anonymous eyewitness describes the rooftop person as wearing all-black tactical gear with a face mask, and says he could not determine race because all skin was covered.
claims.investigative_direction: Cross-reference with police scanner descriptions and the 911 call (A-2141.1); obtain witness's filed written report.

claims.label: Eyewitness Described Rifle as Smaller than Mauser, Resembling .223
claims.claim: In a recording the host plays, the eyewitness says the rooftop person's rifle looked smaller than the recovered Mauser; the host adds that he told her it looked like a .223 and smaller than a .30-06.
claims.investigative_direction: Cross-reference with recovered weapon evidence and any unfired .223 round testimony referenced at 26:40.

claims.label: 911 Caller Reported Person on Building Near Library
claims.claim: In a 911 call the host plays, a voice reports a person on top of a building on the far north side, just east of the library, wearing jeans, a black shirt and a black vest; a second voice repeats it, adding a black mask and a long rifle.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain full 911 transcript and dispatch records for the library area to verify caller statement and subsequent library lockdown.

claims.label: Police Scanner Reported Face Mask and Tactical Gear
claims.claim: In the September 25 recording the host plays, the host says the police scanner described a person in a face mask and tactical gear, while the feds are now saying he wore jeans or something.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain police scanner audio archive and CAD logs from Sept 10 to verify initial dispatch descriptions.

claims.label: Federal Authorities Contacted Eyewitness Only Once; Not Called by Prosecution
claims.claim: The host says the eyewitness was contacted by federal authorities only once, a few days after the incident, and has never been called by the prosecution despite being willing to testify.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain prosecution witness list for Tyler Robinson trial; confirm whether witness was subpoenaed or deposed.

claims.label: Frank Turek Worked as Bank of America Consultant for ~15 Years
claims.claim: Per the Christian Post article (2011) the host reads, Dr. Frank Turek did work on and off for Bank of America for about 15 years, mainly conducting leadership and team-building programs, until being dropped in 2011.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify Bank of America consultancy records and corroborate the 2011 firing and stated reason.

claims.label: Nate Walker: Charlie Chose "Freedom Shirt" Because "Not Controversial"
claims.claim: Nate Walker, Charlie's executive assistant, told Megyn Kelly that Charlie requested the "freedom shirt" from a small selection brought to the event because it "wasn't controversial"; Walker could not recall other shirt options.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain full Megyn Kelly interview and any prior on-record statements by Walker.

claims.label: Comperatore Asserts Butler Shooting Was "Inside Job"
claims.claim: Helen Comperatore stated on NewsNation that she believes the Butler shooter Thomas Crooks was working with someone inside the government, describing it as "an inside job."
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain full NewsNation interview; identify any specific evidence references Comperatore cited ("I've been told things").

claims.label: Comperatore: Secret Service Did Not Reach Out for a Year
claims.claim: In a NewsNation clip the host plays, a reporter says Helen Comperatore says the Secret Service did not reach out to her until a year later and did not fully answer her questions.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain NewsNation transcript and verify Secret Service contact timeline with the Comperatore family.

claims.label: Time Reported Israeli PR Campaign via Clock Tower X Backfired
claims.claim: The host says Time published an article about the Israeli foreign ministry's digital campaign run through Brad Parscale's firm Clock Tower X, and says it seems to have backfired.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain Time article in full; verify spend figures and named individuals (e.g., Eyal Yakoby).

claims.label: Time Reported Campaign Spend of ~$1.5 Million/Day
claims.claim: Per Time article reporting, the Israeli foreign ministry's contracted digital campaign via Clock Tower X was reportedly spending approximately $1.5 million per day.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify the $1.5M/day figure against the Time article text and any underlying contracts/filings cited.

claims.label: Charlie Wore Custom Carhartt Shirt on Sept 10, Not Sold "Freedom Shirt"
claims.claim: Host displays a photo showing Charlie Kirk wearing a customized Carhartt shirt (logo visible) on September 10, distinct from the all-cotton "freedom shirts" sold through TPUSA's for-profit arm after the assassination.
claims.investigative_direction: Identify the vendor/contractor who produced the custom Carhartt shirt and the authorization chain for the custom order.

claims.label: Host Says Silver Alert for Blake Neff's Sept 10 Whereabouts Drew No Tips
claims.claim: The host says that no one reached out to her tip line the previous day in response to her 'silver alert' asking whether anyone saw Blake Neff in Salt Lake City on September 10th.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the prior episode's silver-alert segment and the tip-line inbox log for the period; establish where Neff was on September 10.
claims.transcript_snippet: no one in the entire world reached out to our tip line yesterday in response to our silver alert. No one saw a bald man wandering around looking like he had a bad case of amnesia marking time in Salt Lake City on September 10th.

claims.label: Host Says Chapter Tour Shirts Were Always Provided and Carhartt Is New to TPUSA
claims.claim: The host says that at every Turning Point college stop she did with Charlie Kirk they wore the same t-shirts as the student chapter, provided on arrival, and that she believes Carhartt as a brand is new to TPUSA events.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare photographs of Kirk at earlier campus stops with the September 10 shirt and ask former TPUSA event staff how tour apparel was sourced.
claims.transcript_snippet: At every Turning Point college stop that I ever did with Charlie, we just wore typically the same t-shirts that the student chapter was wearing, and they were provided for us when we arrived.

claims.label: Host Says TPUSA Employees Told Her Carhartt Is Not a Vendor
claims.claim: The host says she asked current and former Turning Point employees whether Carhartt was one of their vendors and was told no.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain TPUSA vendor and purchasing records for apparel and ask the employees on record whether Carhartt ever supplied the organization.
claims.transcript_snippet: I did happen to ask some Turning Point employees, former and current, if Cart Heart was one of their vendors and I was told no

claims.label: Host Asks Viewers for Information on the Custom Shirt via Tip Email
claims.claim: The host asks viewers who know how or whether a single custom shirt was made for Charlie Kirk to email moretips@candaceowens.com.
claims.investigative_direction: Review the tips inbox for responses naming who ordered the custom Carhartt shirt.
claims.transcript_snippet: please do send us an email at moretips@candaceowens. com

claims.label: Host Says Tyler Bowyer's Father Relocated the Family to New Jersey as a Bank of America Executive
claims.claim: The host says Tyler Bowyer's father temporarily moved Tyler and his family to New Jersey during the same period because he served as an executive at Bank of America, and notes that she charted several figures' parents at Bank of America Merrill Lynch.
claims.investigative_direction: Locate employment and residence records for Bowyer's father in New Jersey and the dates of his Bank of America executive role.
claims.transcript_snippet: Tyler Bowyer's dad who temporarily located Tyler and his family to New Jersey during that exact same time frame cuz he needed to serve as an executive to the Bank of America

claims.label: Christian Post Says Turek Was Fired From Cisco Months Before Bank of America
claims.claim: Reading the 2011 Christian Post article, the host says Frank Turek was fired from Cisco Systems in California over an anti-gay-marriage book just months before being given the boot from Bank of America.
claims.investigative_direction: Retrieve the 2011 Christian Post article and contemporaneous coverage of the Cisco dismissal to confirm the sequence and reasons.
claims.transcript_snippet: just months after being fired from Cisco Systems in California over an anti-gay marriage book, Christian consultant Dr. Frank Turek was also given the boot from Bank of America.

claims.label: Article Says Turek Was Hired in May for Bank of America Wealth Management Team and Had Other Clients
claims.claim: The host reads that Turek, a US Navy veteran, was hired in May to present at a meeting of Bank of America's global business management analysis team within global wealth and investment management, and that other clients included Coca-Cola and Home Depot.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify the article text for the hiring month, the division named and the client list.
claims.transcript_snippet: Other clients have included Coca-Cola, Home Depot, among others. The US Navy veteran was hired in May to present at a meeting of Bank of America's global business management analysis team, which is within the global wealth and investment management.

claims.label: Faumuina Does Not Recall Whether Nine Items Were Seized and Agrees Items Went to FBI Lab
claims.claim: Asked whether the seized items numbered nine, Sergeant Faumuina said she did not remember, and she agreed that whatever was seized was sent to the FBI lab.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the hearing transcript and the evidence item log for the library bus stop seizures to establish the item count.
claims.transcript_snippet: Does that ring a bell? >> I don't remember. >> Uh those whatever was seized was sent to the FBI lab for processing. >> Yes.

claims.label: Faumuina Agrees DNA and Other Analysis Was Requested on the Items
claims.claim: In a hearing clip the host plays, Sergeant Faumuina agrees with the questioner that she was requesting both DNA and other types of analysis on the seized items.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the FBI lab request forms and chain-of-custody sheets for the items to see which analyses were requested.
claims.transcript_snippet: Was a decision at some time made and and you were requesting that both DNA and other type of analysis get done? >> Yes.

claims.label: Faumuina Says She Does Not Remember Telling the Lab to Stop but Finds It Consistent With FBI/ATF Notes
claims.claim: Sergeant Faumuina said 'I don't remember communicating that' when asked whether she told the lab the items were unconnected, then said it would not be inconsistent with what she knows if the FBI or ATF notes recorded it, and agreed it would be fair to say the items were determined unrelated.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the FBI and ATF lab notes and reports referenced by the questioner, and the UVU communication that closed the testing request.
claims.transcript_snippet: >> I don't remember communicating that. >> Okay. If that's in the notes of the FBI or the ATF, would that be inconsistent with what you know? >> Uh no.

claims.label: Host Says the Library Is Not Near the Losee Center Route Used in the Questioning
claims.claim: The host says that the questioner had established the person who jumped off the Losee Center ran a particular route, that the library is not near the Losee Center, and that this route is why the abandoned items drew attention.
claims.investigative_direction: Measure the walking distance from the Losee Center to the library bus stops and obtain the hearing testimony that set the route.
claims.transcript_snippet: Just so you guys know, the library is not near Loews Center.

claims.label: Host Says a Source Told Her Early On He Was at the Bus Stop and Filed a Report on the Rooftop Figure
claims.claim: The host says that in her early investigation someone told her he was at the bus stop and made a report about seeing the alleged shooter on the roof, describing the person in all-black tactical gear with every part of the body covered.
claims.investigative_direction: Identify the report this source filed and obtain it from UVU police or the FBI.
claims.transcript_snippet: Back in the early investigation, my early investigation, someone had told me specifically that they were there um by the bus stop, and they actually ended up making a report about having seen the alleged youth shooter, someone on the roof

claims.label: Host Says Temperature Was About 85 Degrees, Making Gloves Notable
claims.claim: The host says it was about 85 degrees in Utah that day, so gloves left at the bus stop are relevant, and she asks who was wearing, holding and dropping gloves and what the other six items were.
claims.investigative_direction: Pull the National Weather Service hourly record for Orem, Utah on September 10, 2025.
claims.transcript_snippet: I think it was literally like 85° in Utah.

claims.label: Host Says the Witness Spoke to Students at the Library Bus Stop and Is the Only Person Who Filmed the Gunman Going Prone
claims.claim: The host says her source spoke to students at the bus stop in front of the library, described the gun, and was the only person who captured the gunman on the Losee Center roof on video as he began lying prone.
claims.investigative_direction: Reconcile with the other rooftop video (the host earlier said two roof videos exist) and obtain both files with metadata.
claims.transcript_snippet: This individual told me that he spoke to students at the bus stop in front of a library and he also described the gun and he was able to do that because he happened to also be the only person who captured the gunman on Losee Center in a video as he began lying prone for the shot.

claims.label: Host Says His Video Was the Most Widely Spread Rooftop Video and the First to Circulate
claims.claim: The host says the witness's clip is the most widely spread video of the alleged shooter on the rooftop and that he was the first to circulate it.
claims.investigative_direction: Trace the earliest posting of the clip and its spread across accounts, using platform timestamps.
claims.transcript_snippet: I'm talking about the wide the most widely spread video of the shooter allegedly on the rooftop. This is He's the first one to have circulated that.

claims.label: Host Says She Tracked Down the Filmer and He Has Never Changed His Description
claims.claim: The host says she tracked down the person who recorded the rooftop footage, has stayed in touch since, and that he has never changed his description of the figure on the roof or the figure running away.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the witness's dated communications with the host and any statements he gave to authorities to test consistency.
claims.transcript_snippet: The person who recorded this footage is the person that I tracked down. It was not easy to track him down, but I've stayed in touch with him since and he has never changed his description

claims.label: Host Says the Witness Filed a Report at the UVU Command Center That the Arrested Man Was Too Old
claims.claim: The host says that after the witness realized police had arrested the wrong person, George Zinn, he walked to the UVU command center and filed a report saying that was not the guy because he was too old.
claims.investigative_direction: Request the UVU command center log and any written report from the afternoon of September 10 under public-records rules.
claims.transcript_snippet: he walked over to the UVU command center and filed a report and said that's not the guy, that can't be the guy. He's just He's too old.

claims.label: Host Says the Witness Works With Guns and Is Willing to Testify
claims.claim: The host says the witness is willing to testify and would be credible because he works with guns.
claims.investigative_direction: Confirm the witness's firearms-related occupation and whether either side has contacted him about testimony.
claims.transcript_snippet: he's also willing to testify. He would be a very credible witness because it happens to be that he works with guns.

claims.label: Witness Says the Shot Came About 5 Seconds After He Stopped Recording
claims.claim: In the recorded call, the witness says the person on the roof fired about 5 seconds after he stopped recording.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare the clip's end time with the audio of the shot in other recordings to check the 5-second gap.
claims.transcript_snippet: about 5 seconds after I stopped recording is when that person fired.

claims.label: Witness Says He Saw No Muzzle Flash and Could Not See the Gun
claims.claim: The witness says he heard and felt everything but did not see a muzzle flash and could not see the gun at the time, only a head and shoulders on the roof.
claims.investigative_direction: Review the roof clip frame by frame for any flash or smoke and compare with expert analysis of visual discharge indicators.
claims.transcript_snippet: I saw heard everything but a muzzle flash. So, I didn't see a flash come from the edge of his gun, as you can [clears throat] see in the video. I couldn't see the gun at the time.

claims.label: Witness Says the Muzzle Report Sounded More Like an AR Than a Large-Bore Hunting Rifle
claims.claim: The witness says the muzzle report sounded more like an AR than a large-bore hunting rifle, while acknowledging he has never heard gunfire around buildings.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain acoustic analysis of audio from several recordings of the shot and the ballistics report for the recovered rifle.
claims.transcript_snippet: it sounded more like a AR than a large bore hunting rifle.

claims.label: Witness Says It Was About 12:20, Not 12:15, and He Saw the Figure for About 30 Seconds
claims.claim: Asked about the federal timing of 12:15 for the person dropping onto the Losee roof, the witness says it was definitely not 12:15 but 12:20 if anything, and that the figure was in view for about 30 seconds.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare the video metadata of the witness's clip with the official 12:15 roof-access time in the charging documents.
claims.transcript_snippet: it was definitely not 12:15. It was It was uh 12:20 if anything. He was He was in our line of view for about 30 seconds total.

claims.label: Witness Says He Assumed the Figure Was an Event Security Guard and Began Recording
claims.claim: The witness says the movement looked tactical, so he started recording because he assumed the person was a security guard heading toward the main tent, and that his video is about 20 seconds with about 10 seconds from the edge of view to the prone position.
claims.investigative_direction: Match the witness's account of a 10-second approach with the roof video and any other camera angles.
claims.transcript_snippet: which is why I started recording because it was I assumed he was a security guard for the event.

claims.label: Witness Says the Figure Fired Then Lay About 5 Seconds Before Sprinting Off the Roof
claims.claim: The witness says the figure was in position about 20 seconds while he filmed, fired about 5 seconds after the video ended, stayed on the ground about 5 more seconds, then stood and sprinted off the roof.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare against the court-shown rooftop video and the dispatch time of the first shots-fired call.
claims.transcript_snippet: And then firing, he was maybe on the ground for 5 more seconds before he stood up and absolutely sprinted off the roof.

claims.label: Witness Says He Was About 175 Yards From the Figure
claims.claim: The witness says he was about 175 yards from the person on the roof and has since checked the distance on Google Maps.
claims.investigative_direction: Measure the distance from the witness's vantage location to the Losee Center roof edge using mapping and survey data.
claims.transcript_snippet: At the range we were at, we were about 175 yd from him.
